summary_out.changed: Replaced g1l2's static [0.30, 0.70] imbalance thresholds with an adaptive rolling-quantile imbalance gate (p10/p90 over the same 60s window the spread gate uses), and added per-gate skip counters (skipped_position/spread/imbalance_buy/imbalance_sell) emitted via self.log.info in on_stop. Position-cap and rolling-spread-p75 gates from g1l1 are preserved unchanged.
summary_out.outcome: pnl +26.55% vs position-tier-gate (5394.25 vs 4262.50), sharpe 23.17, trade_count 87319, drawdown -0.00610 — bit-for-bit identical to ptg-isl-g1l1 AND ptg-isl-g1l2 on every reported metric (PnL, trade_count, sharpe, drawdown, win_rate, is_weighted_bps). Second consecutive null result for the imbalance branch of this lineage: two mechanically distinct imbalance gates (static thresholds and adaptive quantiles) both produced zero incremental effect on top of g1l1's spread+cap stack. The +26.55% lift is entirely inherited from g1l1. Gate skip counters were NOT recovered: scripts/run_research_backtest.py does not capture subprocess stdout, so self.log.info lines emitted in on_stop are discarded — the diagnostic the loop was designed to provide is unobtainable from the persisted artifacts.
summary_out.hypothesis: Static [0.30, 0.70] thresholds in g1l2 might have been too extreme for the q distribution that survives the spread+cap gates; a rolling-quantile gate self-calibrates to fire on ~10% of BUYs/SELLs regardless of the absolute imbalance level on the surviving slice. Persisted gate counters would also let future loops distinguish 'gate never fires' from 'gate fires but is EV-neutral'.
summary_out.next: Highest-leverage move for g1l4 and for other islands considering imbalance-style gates: (1) persist per-gate skip counters to a JSON sidecar in on_stop (results/<date>/gate-counters.json) — subprocess log output is not captured, so without on-disk persistence every gate experiment on this base is undiagnosable; (2) abandon the imbalance axis on this base — two consecutive null diffs (static + adaptive) strongly suggest queue imbalance on the surviving slice carries no exploitable EV on position-tier-gate, and continued imbalance-gate variations are not the highest-leverage path. Promising orthogonal axes to try instead: short-horizon realized vol (skip OPENs during quiet/dead periods), trade-intensity bursts, or per-tier position-aware sizing instead of binary gating. Other islands evaluating gate-stacking on different bases should NOT assume imbalance gating works just because spread gating does — orthogonality of microstructure features depends on which prior gates the surviving order slice has already been through.
